newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal prices fall on increased arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal prices fall on increased arrivals.

text.p: Indian soymeal export prices, for November shipments, have dipped by nearly $17 per tonne during the last 10 days due to increased arrivals of the new soybean crop, traders said on Friday.
They said soymeal exporters were currently signing contracts at $258 per tonne fob for November shipments compared to around $275 ten days ago.
New soybean, of around 5,000 tonnes per day, had started arriving in the markets in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, the hub of India's soybean indutry.
"Due to additional availability of soybean there is currently no premium on soymeal," said Sunil Saboo of S.S. Merchantile, a leading oilmeal broker.
Traders said Indian soymeal exporters had signed deals to export nearly 550,000 tonnes of soymeal for November, December and January shipments.
Soybean was quoted at around 9,700-10,000 rupees per tonne in the domestic markets. In plant delivery conditions it was quoted at around 9,850-10,250 rupees per tonne.
